title: Microsoft PL-300 Power BI Data Analyst Study Guide
description: PL-300 earns Microsoft Certified: Power BI Data Analyst Associate. The exam covers the full Power BI workflow — preparing data, modelling it, visualising and analysing it, and managing and securing workspaces — with Power Query and DAX proficiency assumed throughout. It is a practitioner exam: the questions describe a business requirement and ask which modelling or visual choice satisfies it, not what a button is called.
audience: Data analysts and reporting specialists who already build in Power BI, finance and operations people who have become their team's de facto analyst, and anyone whose organisation runs Microsoft's data stack. You are expected to work with business stakeholders to pin down requirements and with data engineers to get at the data — and to be genuinely comfortable in Power Query and DAX, which is where most candidates lose marks.
why_get_it: Power BI is the most widely deployed BI tool in the enterprise, and PL-300 is the credential hiring managers recognize for it. It appears by name in job listings for Data Analyst, BI Analyst, BI Developer, and Reporting Analyst roles—especially at companies already invested in Microsoft 365 and Azure. Unlike vendor-neutral analytics credentials, PL-300 tests hands-on tool skills: Power Query transformations, star-schema modeling, DAX measures (CALCULATE, time intelligence), and service-side administration like row-level security and scheduled refresh. That specificity is its value—passing it signals you can actually build and ship reports, not just talk about analytics concepts. The exam was refreshed in April 2026 and now includes Copilot-assisted report building and DirectLake, so the current version reflects how Power BI is genuinely used today. It will not get you hired on its own—a portfolio of real reports matters at least as much—but combined with demonstrable work, it gets you past resume filters in Microsoft shops.
when_to_get_it: Take PL-300 once you have built real reports that other people use, because the exam rewards that and punishes tutorial-only preparation. It is the strongest single credential for a Power BI job, and it is the natural follow-on to the Google Data Analytics or Business Intelligence certificates, which teach the craft but carry no proctored exam. Power BI Desktop is free, so the practice costs nothing but time. If your target work is SQL and pipelines rather than reporting, DP-203 or a cloud data engineering path fits better.
salary_note: Entry-level data analyst and reporting analyst roles typically start in the $60K–$75K range in the U.S. Mid-level BI analyst and BI developer roles commonly reach $80K–$100K, and senior BI developers with strong DAX and SQL frequently exceed $110K. Be realistic: PL-300 alone does not command a premium—employers pay for the combination of the credential, a portfolio of real reports, and SQL skills. It functions as a door-opener, not a salary lever.
exam_format: Multiple choice, multiple select, drag-and-drop and other interactive types, sometimes including a case study. Microsoft schedules associate exams at 100 minutes (120 minutes of seat time) and does not publish a fixed question count — most of its exams run 40 to 60 questions. Passing score: 700 on a scale of 100–1000. Proctored through Pearson VUE, at a test centre or online.
exam_questions: 40–60 questions typically (Microsoft does not publish an exact count)
recertification_note: The Microsoft Certified: Power BI Data Analyst Associate certification is valid for one year, and renewal is free: pass a short, unproctored, open-book assessment on Microsoft Learn during the six-month window before your expiry date. You can retake the assessment as often as you need, and passing extends the certification another year. Miss the window and the certification lapses — you sit the full exam again.

items: Connecting to data sources and shared semantic models
Choosing between Import, DirectQuery, and DirectLake storage modes
Profiling data: column statistics, nulls, and data quality issues
Power Query transformations: merge, append, pivot/unpivot, grouping
Building fact and dimension tables with appropriate keys
Star-schema design: relationships, cardinality, cross-filter direction
Common date tables and role-playing dimensions
DAX measures: CALCULATE, time intelligence, semi-additive measures
Calculated columns, calculated tables, and calculation groups
Performance tuning with Performance Analyzer and DAX query view
Choosing and configuring visuals, themes, and conditional formatting
Bookmarks, drillthrough, sync slicers, and report navigation
Copilot features: narrative visuals and report page suggestions
AI visuals, forecasting, reference lines, and anomaly detection
Accessibility, mobile layouts, and paginated report use cases
Workspaces, apps, and content distribution methods
Scheduled refresh, gateways, and semantic model settings
Row-level security roles and group membership
Item-level access and semantic model permissions
Sensitivity labels and content endorsement (promote/certify)

study_steps.title: Download the official study guide
study_steps.description: Start with Microsoft's official PL-300 study guide, which lists every skill measured with current weightings. The exam was updated April 20, 2026 (Copilot features and DirectLake are now in scope), so ignore any prep material that still references 'Deploy and maintain assets' as the fourth domain—it is now 'Manage and secure Power BI.'

study_steps.title: Work through the free Microsoft Learn path
study_steps.description: Microsoft Learn's free self-paced PL-300 modules cover every exam domain and are the single best-aligned resource because Microsoft writes both the modules and the exam. Do the exercises, not just the reading—the exam tests applied skills like choosing the right transformation or storage mode.

study_steps.title: Build real reports with real data
study_steps.description: Power BI Desktop is free. Pick a dataset you actually care about, pull it through Power Query, model it as a star schema, and publish it to the service. The exam's scenario questions assume you have felt the difference between a calculated column and a measure, and know what breaks when relationships are set wrong. Two or three end-to-end projects also become your portfolio—which matters more to employers than the cert itself.

study_steps.title: Go deep on DAX and data modeling
study_steps.description: DAX is where most candidates lose points. CALCULATE and filter context, time intelligence functions, and semi-additive measures all appear on the exam. SQLBI's free articles and videos are the best DAX resource anywhere. Do not memorize function signatures—understand evaluation context, because the questions are written to punish surface-level memorization.

study_steps.title: Take the free official practice assessment
study_steps.description: Microsoft provides a free official practice assessment for PL-300 on Microsoft Learn. Take it early to find weak domains, then again after targeted review. It mirrors the real exam's style and wording. If you want more question volume, add a paid practice exam set, but do the free official one first.

study_steps.title: Drill your weak domains systematically
study_steps.description: Score each practice attempt by domain and review every wrong answer until you understand why the right answer wins and each distractor fails. The four domains are weighted almost evenly, so you cannot afford to write off any of them. Manage and Secure Power BI is the smallest domain but frequently neglected—know your workspace roles and row-level security cold.

study_steps.title: Schedule and sit the exam
study_steps.description: Book through Pearson VUE, in person or online proctored. You get 100 minutes; budget extra time for case-study questions. If you fail, you can retake after 24 hours (waiting periods increase for later attempts). Check for discounts before paying full price—Microsoft Virtual Training Days and student pricing regularly cut the fee substantially.

faq.question: Is the PL-300 certification worth it?
faq.answer: If you are targeting data analyst or BI roles at companies using Microsoft tools, yes—it is the credential recruiters search for when hiring Power BI analysts. It is less useful if your target employers run Tableau or Looker. Be clear-eyed about what it does: it gets you past resume filters and validates tool skills, but employers hire on the combination of the cert, a portfolio of real reports, and usually SQL. On its own it guarantees nothing.

faq.question: How hard is the PL-300 exam?
faq.answer: Moderately hard. It assumes real working familiarity with Power BI—candidates who only watched videos without building reports commonly fail. DAX questions (filter context, time intelligence) and the scenario-based format are the main difficulty. Most candidates with some Power BI exposure need 4–8 weeks of part-time study; complete beginners should plan for 2–3 months including hands-on practice.

faq.question: How much does the PL-300 exam cost?
faq.answer: $165 USD in the United States; pricing varies by country. Students can get academic pricing in most countries, and Microsoft regularly offers 50% or 100% discount vouchers through Virtual Training Days and promotional sweepstakes—check for those before paying full price. If you fail, retakes cost full price each time, though Exam Replay bundles with a retake are sometimes available.

faq.question: Does PL-300 expire? What does renewal cost?
faq.answer: The certification is valid for 12 months, but renewal is free and easy: pass an online, unproctored assessment on Microsoft Learn any time in the six months before expiration. You can retake the renewal assessment as often as needed at no cost. This is genuinely one of the friendliest renewal models in the industry—just set a calendar reminder, because a lapsed certification requires retaking the full exam.

faq.question: Do I need experience before taking PL-300?
faq.answer: There are no formal prerequisites, but Microsoft's audience profile assumes proficiency with Power Query and DAX. Practically, you should have built several reports end-to-end—from connecting to data through publishing and sharing—before sitting the exam. Excel power users with PivotTable and Power Query experience adapt fastest since Power BI uses the same underlying engines.

faq.question: What jobs can I get with PL-300?
faq.answer: Data Analyst, Business Intelligence Analyst, BI Developer, Reporting Analyst, and Analytics Consultant roles commonly list PL-300 as a requirement or preference—especially at Microsoft-stack companies and consultancies. It pairs almost universally with SQL requirements, so build SQL skills alongside it. It is not a data engineering or data science credential; for those paths look at Fabric and Azure data certifications instead.

faq.question: Is PL-300 the same as the old DA-100 exam?
faq.answer: PL-300 replaced DA-100 in 2022; the certification title (Power BI Data Analyst Associate) is the same. The exam content has been updated several times since—most recently April 2026, when the fourth domain became 'Manage and secure Power BI' and Copilot-assisted report building and DirectLake entered the objectives. Make sure any course or practice exam you buy has been updated for the current objectives, not DA-100-era content.
